newsitem.title: USA: ELEK-TEK hires advisor, mulls options.
newsitem.headline: ELEK-TEK hires advisor, mulls options.

text.p: ELEK-TEK Inc said Tuesday it hired ABN AMRO Chicago Corp as its financial advisor and is exploring business options including the possible sale of the company.
"ELEK-TEK's most important objective is maximizing value for the company's shareholders," said chairman Robert Lipsig in a statement.

He said ELEK-TEK and its advisor will explore a range of alternatives, including additional capital, the possibility of a sale of the company, a merger or other form of business combination or affiliation.

In the second half of 1996, ELEK-TEK undertook several initiatives aimed at improving its profitability. Management's efforts included refocusing the company's business strategy, improving inventory management, pursuing administrative cost savings, and reducing professional fees.
These changes have helped position ELEK-TEK for the future," Richard L. Rodriguez, president and chief executive officer, commented.

ELEK-TEK, with 1996 sales of $333.5 million, markets microcomputer products through a multi-channel distribution system including eight retail stores, a national catalog sales operation; and direct sales divisions serving corporate, educational and government customers.
Earlier this month, the company said it was in violation of certain covenants of a lending agreement with its principal lenders as a result of its 1996 fourth quarter loss of $4 million.
